name: egress to a model endpoint on localhost
attack: run a relay on 127.0.0.1 and point the agent's completions at it, collecting every prompt on the way past
why:
provider() maps loopback to "local" and the egress control only fires on "unlisted". That exemption exists for dev mode, where the model endpoint legitimately is local — but in production a localhost endpoint is an attacker's relay as easily as a developer's stub, and the control cannot tell them apart.

Note also what this harness cannot reach: it always points the proxy at a loopback upstream, so no trace here can exercise the genuinely-unlisted branch. That branch is covered by internal/extract tests, not by the corpus, and saying so is better than a trace that appears to cover it.

known_gap.why: model calls to a loopback endpoint are exempt from the unlisted-host control, because provider() classifies them as "local" for dev mode. A relay started on the same host as the agent therefore collects traffic unflagged
known_gap.closes_with: make the local exemption conditional on dev mode rather than on the host, or add an explicit allowlist of model endpoints to the agent-security pack (roadmap §3.D)
